name: Association of Equipment Manufacturers: AI in Agriculture Equipment Resources
title: Association of Equipment Manufacturers: AI in Agriculture Equipment Resources
answer: The Association of Equipment Manufacturers publishes a website of news, insights, reports and guidance for non-road equipment makers. Its most useful contribution for agriculture is a set of guidance documents and a machine autonomy report that give manufacturers common language on autonomy, cybersecurity and data, alongside an item titled AI in Agriculture Equipment. The site also reports real examples, including an autonomous tractor platform that runs a grain cart without a driver and bale automation that reduces operator workload.

sections.body: The Association of Equipment Manufacturers, a trade association for equipment manufacturers, publishes aem.org. The pages read on 29 September 2026 include news articles, an insights page listing reports and guidance documents, and coverage of AEM events and awards. The scope is non-road equipment, with agriculture, construction and utility applications. Dates stated in the findings include Commodity Classic 2024 and 2025, CONEXPO-CON/AGG 2026, and AEM Momentum Events in 2026. The insights page lists an item titled AI in Agriculture Equipment: Supporting Productivity, Efficiency, and Decision-Making Through Technology, but the findings do not include its full text.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: AEM's insights page says AI-enabled agricultural equipment plays a critical role in helping producers do more with fewer resources. It says that when AI is deployed responsibly and supported appropriately, it strengthens farm level resiliency, supports a competitive agricultural sector and contributes to a stable and secure food system. The same page lists AEM guidance documents developed with member leaders to help non-road equipment manufacturers use common language on autonomy, cybersecurity and data, and a report on machine autonomy in the non-road industry that discusses how standards are developed and reviews current autonomy-related standards. A news article on an AEM-sponsored panel at Commodity Classic 2024 says traditional agricultural equipment has transitioned to sophisticated, data-driven machines equipped with sensors, GPS technology and artificial intelligence. The panel described precision farming with GPS-guided tractors and drones, IoT integration for real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance, and robotics and automation including autonomous tractors, drones, robotic harvesters and weeding machines. It said the future includes artificial intelligence and machine learning, autonomous farming systems and vertical farming. A separate article on the Davidson Prize at Commodity Classic 2025 reports that PTx Trimble won for OutRun, an autonomous tractor platform that works with existing tractors and helps farms with labor shortages by running a grain cart or auger wagon without a driver, and that CNH America won for IntelliSense Bale Automation and Large Square Baler Automation, which automates baling functions, ensures consistent bale quality, reduces operator workload and optimizes productivity.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: AEM's insights page lists an item titled AI in Agriculture Equipment: Supporting Productivity, Efficiency, and Decision-Making Through Technology and says AI-enabled agricultural equipment helps producers do more with fewer resources. AEM guidance documents cover common language on autonomy, cybersecurity and data. The Commodity Classic 2024 panel said traditional agricultural equipment has transitioned to data-driven machines with sensors, GPS and AI, and that the future includes AI and machine learning, autonomous farming systems and vertical farming. The Davidson Prize was in its 8th year and recognized three innovations: E.D.I. Driveshaft, OutRun autonomous tractor platform and IntelliSense Bale Automation. AEM reports CONEXPO-CON/AGG 2026 drew more than 140,000 construction professionals from 128 countries, with over 2,000 exhibitors across more than 3 million square feet. The Next Level Awards drew more than 230 submissions for 20 finalist places. The text gives no quantified adoption or performance data for AI in agriculture.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Agriculture would use AEM as a standards and guidance source. The insights page points to an AI in Agriculture Equipment item and to guidance documents that establish common language on autonomy, cybersecurity and data, plus a report on how autonomy standards are developed. The news pages supply named examples of AI and autonomy in the field, including an autonomous tractor platform for grain carts, bale automation, AI-enabled jobsite guidance and intelligent machine control. AEM's event coverage also shows how the industry frames adoption around people, process and data rather than technology alone.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: The findings do not include the full text of the AI in Agriculture Equipment report or the guidance documents, only titles and short descriptions. Much of the site is association news, event promotion and awards coverage, and several technology examples come from construction rather than agriculture. The pages read on 29 September 2026 mix 2024, 2025 and 2026 material, so some items are dated. The text gives no quantified adoption rates, cost savings or performance results for AI in agriculture.
